### Clone Agent Chat UI Repository Source: https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/langgraph/ui Clone the Agent Chat UI repository from GitHub, install its dependencies, and start the development server for local customization. ```bash # Clone the repository git clone https://github.com/langchain-ai/agent-chat-ui.git cd agent-chat-ui # Install dependencies and start pnpm install pnpm dev ``` -------------------------------- ### Create Agent Chat UI Project with npx Source: https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/langgraph/ui Use npx to scaffold a new Agent Chat UI project, install its dependencies, and start the development server. ```bash # Create a new Agent Chat UI project npx create-agent-chat-app --project-name my-chat-ui cd my-chat-ui # Install dependencies and start pnpm install pnpm dev ``` -------------------------------- ### Send Message to Assistant (Sync Python SDK) Source: https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/langgraph/local-server Use the synchronous LangGraph Python SDK client to send a message to an assistant on a local server and stream the response. This client operates in a blocking manner. ```python from langgraph_sdk import get_sync_client client = get_sync_client(url="http://localhost:2024") for chunk in client.runs.stream( None, # Threadless run "agent", # Name of assistant. Defined in langgraph.json. input={ "messages": [{ "role": "human", "content": "What is LangGraph?", }], }, stream_mode="messages-tuple", ): print(f"Receiving new event of type: {chunk.event}...") print(chunk.data) print("\n\n") ``` -------------------------------- ### Send Message to Assistant (Async Python SDK) Source: https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/langgraph/local-server Use the asynchronous LangGraph Python SDK client to send a message to an assistant on a local server and stream the response. This requires an async context. ```python from langgraph_sdk import get_client import asyncio client = get_client(url="http://localhost:2024") async def main(): async for chunk in client.runs.stream( None, # Threadless run "agent", # Name of assistant. Defined in langgraph.json. input={ "messages": [{ "role": "human", "content": "What is LangGraph?", }], }, ): print(f"Receiving new event of type: {chunk.event}...") print(chunk.data) print("\n\n") asyncio.run(main()) ``` -------------------------------- ### POST /runs/stream Source: https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/langgraph/local-server Sends a message to the assistant for a threadless run and streams the response. This endpoint allows direct interaction with the LangGraph agent. ```APIDOC ## POST /runs/stream ### Description Sends a message to the assistant for a threadless run and streams the response. ### Method POST ### Endpoint /runs/stream ### Parameters #### Request Body - **assistant_id** (string) - Required - The name of the assistant, as defined in langgraph.json. - **input** (object) - Required - The input payload for the assistant. - **messages** (array of objects) - Required - A list of message objects. - **role** (string) - Required - The role of the message sender (e.g., "human"). - **content** (string) - Required - The content of the message. - **stream_mode** (string) - Optional - Specifies the streaming mode for the response (e.g., "messages-tuple"). ### Request Example ```json { "assistant_id": "agent", "input": { "messages": [ { "role": "human", "content": "What is LangGraph?" } ] }, "stream_mode": "messages-tuple" } ``` ``` -------------------------------- ### Send Message to Assistant (REST API) Source: https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/langgraph/local-server Send a message to the local LangGraph server's REST API using cURL. This example demonstrates how to stream responses directly from the HTTP endpoint. ```bash curl -s --request POST \ --url "http://localhost:2024/runs/stream" \ --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \ --data "{ \"assistant_id\": \"agent\", \"input\": { \"messages\": [ { \"role\": \"human\", \"content\": \"What is LangGraph?\" } ] }, \"stream_mode\": \"messages-tuple\" }" ``` -------------------------------- ### Disable streaming for specific chat models Source: https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/langgraph/streaming Set streaming=False when initializing the model. If a model integration does not support the streaming parameter, use disable_streaming=True instead. ```python from langchain.chat_models import init_chat_model model = init_chat_model( "claude-sonnet-4-6", # Set streaming=False to disable streaming for the chat model streaming=False # [!code highlight] ) ``` ```python from langchain_openai import ChatOpenAI # Set streaming=False to disable streaming for the chat model model = ChatOpenAI(model="gpt-5.5", streaming=False) ``` -------------------------------- ### Extended example of streaming an arbitrary chat model Source: https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/langgraph/streaming Define a tool-calling graph that streams tokens from an external OpenAI client using a custom stream writer, and invoke it using astream with stream_mode='custom'. ```python import operator import json from typing import TypedDict from typing_extensions import Annotated from langgraph.graph import StateGraph, START from openai import AsyncOpenAI openai_client = AsyncOpenAI() model_name = "gpt-5.4-mini" async def stream_tokens(model_name: str, messages: list[dict]): response = await openai_client.chat.completions.create( messages=messages, model=model_name, stream=True ) role = None async for chunk in response: delta = chunk.choices[0].delta if delta.role is not None: role = delta.role if delta.content: yield {"role": role, "content": delta.content} # this is our tool async def get_items(place: str) -> str: """Use this tool to list items one might find in a place you're asked about.""" writer = get_stream_writer() response = "" async for msg_chunk in stream_tokens( model_name, [ { "role": "user", "content": ( "Can you tell me what kind of items " f"i might find in the following place: '{place}'. " "List at least 3 such items separating them by a comma. " "And include a brief description of each item." ), } ], ): response += msg_chunk["content"] writer(msg_chunk) return response class State(TypedDict): messages: Annotated[list[dict], operator.add] # this is the tool-calling graph node async def call_tool(state: State): ai_message = state["messages"][-1] tool_call = ai_message["tool_calls"][-1] function_name = tool_call["function"]["name"] if function_name != "get_items": raise ValueError(f"Tool {function_name} not supported") function_arguments = tool_call["function"]["arguments"] arguments = json.loads(function_arguments) function_response = await get_items(**arguments) tool_message = { "tool_call_id": tool_call["id"], "role": "tool", "name": function_name, "content": function_response, } return {"messages": [tool_message]} graph = ( StateGraph(State) .add_node(call_tool) .add_edge(START, "call_tool") .compile() ) ``` ```python inputs = { "messages": [ { "content": None, "role": "assistant", "tool_calls": [ { "id": "1", "function": { "arguments": '{"place":"bedroom"}', "name": "get_items", }, "type": "function", } ], } ] } async for chunk in graph.astream( inputs, stream_mode="custom", version="v2", ): if chunk["type"] == "custom": print(chunk["data"]["content"], end="|", flush=True) ``` -------------------------------- ### Start LangGraph Development Server Source: https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/langgraph/studio Use this command to start the local development server, making your LangGraph agent accessible via API and the Studio UI. For Safari users, consider using `--tunnel` to work around localhost connection issues. ```shell langgraph dev ``` -------------------------------- ### LangSmith Studio URL for Local Server Source: https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/langgraph/local-server The URL to access the LangSmith Studio UI, pre-configured to connect to the locally running LangGraph API server. ```text > - LangGraph Studio Web UI: https://smith.langchain.com/studio/?baseUrl=http://127.0.0.1:2024 ``` -------------------------------- ### Install LangGraph CLI for Agent Server Source: https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/langgraph/studio Install the LangGraph CLI, which provides a local development server to connect your agent to Studio. Python 3.11 or higher is required. ```shell pip install --upgrade "langgraph-cli[inmem]" ``` -------------------------------- ### Agent Tool Execution and Invocation Source: https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/langgraph/quickstart This snippet demonstrates the core loop for executing tools within a LangGraph agent and invoking the agent to stream events. It shows how tool results are integrated back into the message history. ```python # Execute tools tool_result_futures = [ call_tool(tool_call) for tool_call in model_response.tool_calls ] tool_results = [fut.result() for fut in tool_result_futures] messages = add_messages(messages, [model_response, *tool_results]) model_response = call_llm(messages).result() messages = add_messages(messages, model_response) return messages # Invoke messages = [HumanMessage(content="Add 3 and 4.")] stream = agent.stream_events(messages, version="v3") for snapshot in stream.values: print(snapshot) print("\n") ``` -------------------------------- ### Normalize Agent Server Base URL Function Source: https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/langgraph/frontend/custom-stream-channels This function normalizes the agent server base URL based on input parameters, supporting local preview and production environments. ```javascript function normalizeAgentServerBase(agentServer, useLocalPreview) { const trimmed = agentServer.trim(); if (useLocalPreview) { return "http://127.0.0.1:2024"; } if (trimmed === "prod") { return PROD_AGENT_API_BASE; } if (trimmed === "local") { return PROD_AGENT_API_BASE; } return PROD_AGENT_API_BASE; } ``` -------------------------------- ### Handle Interrupts in Subagent Invocations in Python Source: https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/langgraph/use-subgraphs Shows how to stream events from an agent invocation, detect an interrupt from a subagent's tool call, and then resume the execution by approving the interrupt. ```python from langgraph.types import Command config = {"configurable": {"thread_id": "1"}} # Stream events - the subagent's tool calls interrupt() stream = agent.stream_events( {"messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Tell me about apples"}]}, config=config, version="v3", ) output = stream.output # drive the stream to completion # stream.interrupts contains pending interrupts (and stream.interrupted is True) # Resume - approve the interrupt resumed = agent.stream_events(Command(resume=True), config=config, version="v3") final = resumed.output ``` -------------------------------- ### Stream Agent Events for Human Review (Python) Source: https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/langgraph/sql-agent This Python snippet demonstrates how to stream events from an agent, enabling human-in-the-loop review. It shows how to resume an interrupted stream with an 'accept' command and process the agent's output. ```python from langgraph.types import Command stream = agent.stream_events( Command(resume={"type": "accept"}), # Command(resume={"type": "edit", "args": {"query": "..."}}), config, version="v3", ) for message in stream.messages: for token in message.text: print(token, end="", flush=True) if stream.interrupted: action = stream.interrupts[0] print("INTERRUPTED:") for request in action.value: print(json.dumps(request, indent=2)) ``` -------------------------------- ### Define Per-Thread Fruit Expert Subagent Source: https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/langgraph/use-subgraphs This snippet defines a fruit expert subagent with per-thread persistence enabled via `checkpointer=True`. It also shows how to wrap this subagent as a tool for an outer agent, emphasizing the use of `ToolCallLimitMiddleware` to prevent parallel calls to per-thread subagents. ```python from langchain.agents import create_agent from langchain.agents.middleware import ToolCallLimitMiddleware from langchain.tools import tool from langgraph.checkpoint.memory import MemorySaver from langgraph.types import Command, interrupt @tool def fruit_info(fruit_name: str) -> str: """Look up fruit info.""" return f"Info about {fruit_name}" # Subagent with checkpointer=True for persistent state fruit_agent = create_agent( model="gpt-5.4-mini", tools=[fruit_info], prompt="You are a fruit expert. Use the fruit_info tool. Respond in one sentence.", checkpointer=True # [!code highlight] ) # Wrap subagent as a tool for the outer agent @tool def ask_fruit_expert(question: str) -> str: """Ask the fruit expert. Use for ALL fruit questions.""" response = fruit_agent.invoke( {"messages": [{"role": "user", "content": question}]}, ) return response["messages"][-1].content # Outer agent with checkpointer ``` -------------------------------- ### Initialize useStream for Graph Execution in Frontend Frameworks Source: https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/langgraph/frontend/graph-execution Initialize `useStream` (or `injectStream` for Angular) with the agent's API URL and assistant ID to manage stream state and access discovered graph nodes for UI components. ```tsx import { useStream } from "@langchain/react"; const AGENT_URL = "http://localhost:2024"; export function PipelineChat() { const stream = useStream({ apiUrl: AGENT_URL, assistantId: "graph_execution_cards", }); const graphNodes = [...stream.subgraphs.values()]; return (
); } ``` ```vue ``` ```svelte

function normalizeAgentServerBase(agentServer, useLocalPreview) { const trimmed = agentServer.trim(); if (useLocalPreview) { return "http://127.0.0.1:2024"; } if (trimmed === "prod") { return PROD_AGENT_API_BASE; } if (trimmed === "local") { return PROD_AGENT_API_BASE; } return PROD_AGENT_API_BASE; } ``` -------------------------------- ### Multi-Turn Agent Conversation Source: https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/langgraph/use-subgraphs Illustrates how an agent accumulates state across multiple invocations, allowing it to remember past conversations and maintain context in multi-turn interactions. ```python config = {"configurable": {"thread_id": "1"}} # First call response = agent.invoke( {"messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Tell me about apples"}]}, config=config, ) # Subagent message count: 4 # Second call - subagent REMEMBERS apples conversation response = agent.invoke( {"messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Now tell me about bananas"}]}, config=config, ) # Subagent message count: 8 (accumulated!) ```
